scone.prep: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
scone.cook: Arrange the scones about 5 cm (2 in) apart on the sheet. Bake at {temp} for {time}, until risen and golden brown on top.
scone.check: The tops should be golden and a toothpick inserted into the thickest part should come out clean.
notes: @butter: Cold butter and a hot oven give tall, flaky scones.
Scones are best eaten warm on the day they are baked.

scone.prep: Line the basket with perforated air fryer parchment, or lightly grease it.
scone.cook: Place 3-4 scones in the basket with space between them. Air fry at {temp} for {time}, until risen and golden.
scone.check: The tops should be golden and a toothpick inserted into the thickest part should come out clean. If they brown too fast, cover loosely with foil.
notes: Air fryers vary a lot - start checking at the early end of the range.
Do not crowd the basket; scones need room to rise.

recipes.name: Classic Scones
recipes.description: Tender, buttery scones with a golden top.

yield.note: Based on one round of dough cut into 8 wedges.

less.note: Scones are only lightly sweet by design, so about 25% less sugar still tastes good - especially with jam or cream.
expectedChanges: Crumb may be a little less tender

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the {L|=flour;#granulated_sugar|sugar;#baking_powder|baking powder;=salt}.

steps.title: Cut In the {^butter|Butter}
steps.text: Rub or cut the {@butter|cold butter} into the dry ingredients with your fingertips or a pastry cutter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces.

steps.title: Add the Wet Ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the {L|#egg|egg;#heavy_cream|cream} together, pour into the dry mixture and stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it into a round about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick - knead only 2-3 times. Cut into wedges (about 4 for every cup of flour) and brush the tops with a little {#heavy_cream|cream} or milk.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the scones cool on the sheet for 5-10 minutes before serving.

tips: @butter: Keep the butter cold - warm butter melts into the flour and makes flat, tough scones.
Handle the dough as little as possible.
Cut straight down with a knife - do not twist, or the scones will not rise evenly.
